notes: The pattern accepts the shared repository's raw-main or raw-tag `fhgff3.json` URL (under either the current or the former repository name) and a `https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fhgff3/vX.Y.Z` alias. Cite the release a file targets.
`schema` also identifies the header type (requirement FR-010).
`1.1` came with shared release v0.5.0; `1.0` was first released in v0.4.0. Quote it in YAML.

A schema of version M.N also accepts records that state an earlier minor, and holds each of them to that minor: an `x-` extension field is valid only in a record that states `1.1`, exactly as it would be invalid under the 1.0 schema (docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md).
Required and non-empty for a conforming record, even though `""` passes the released schema.

Must carry a non-empty `name` or `uri`; a required `taxon.uri` is decided for the next major (FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#189). `##species` directives in the same file are compared by the gff3-validator, not by the schema.
Version of the annotation, not of the genome it annotates and not `schemaVersion`.
Required and non-empty for a conforming record; every author needs a non-empty `name`.

metadataAuthor[].uri.exampleLabel: ORCID URI used by the released family examples

checksum.units: standard padded base64 of the SHA-512/256 digest
notes: Covers every byte of the GFF3 file — native directives, features and any `##FASTA` section — except the root `#~checksum:` line (rules R1 to R4).
Sorting or tidying the GFF3 (for example `gt gff3 -sort -tidy`) changes bytes, so the copied header no longer verifies. Nothing repairs it.

accessionID.name.exampleLabel: placeholder value; no released FHGFF3 example states an accessionID

scholarlyArticle.units: DOI suffix (bare DOI, no resolver prefix)

notes: Rule R14: validators warn about unusual URI schemes but such a value stays valid; JSON-LD and schema.org writers refuse to emit it as a link.

annotationProtocol.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example

annotationSoftware[].name.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example

annotationSoftware[].version.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example

annotationSoftware[].commandLineOption.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example

soVersion.units: Sequence Ontology release, as its data-version
soVersion.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example
notes: A free-text version string in the schema: it states which SO release the feature types follow, and the gff3-validator does terms against its own SO data.
Counts asserted by the producer, per feature type as written in column 3. They are not recounted by the schema.

featureCounts[].featureType.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example
featureCounts[].featureType.units: SO term name or accession, as written in column 3

featureCounts[].count.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example

notes: The weaker of the two genome links: an identity asserted by the producer, never checksum-verified (requirement FR-006). Prefer `derivedFrom` with `annotates` when the genome file itself carries an FHR header.
`^\S+$` only: any non-space token is accepted, so a nonsense accession still validates.
Supplied, not computed. `bioheaders verify-links` can compare it against the SeqCol digest an FHR header records for the genome.

genomeReference.assemblyName.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example
notes: Compare with the file's own `##genome-build` directive: a disagreement is reported as a warning by the gff3-validator (HDR-010), not as a schema error.

completeness.lineageDataset.exampleLabel: lineage named by the released FHGFF3 example
completeness.lineageDataset.units: BUSCO lineage dataset name including its `odb` version suffix
notes: The pattern allows `_odb` plus digits only, so a dotted dataset version such as `odb12.2` has no typed slot (FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#170).

completeness.completeSingle.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example

completeness.completeDuplicated.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example

completeness.fragmented.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example

completeness.missing.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example

completeness.total.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example

notes: The strong genome link. `bioheaders verify-links annotation.fhgff3.gff3 genome.fhr.fasta` recomputes the parent's checksum and reports `matched`, `not matched` or `not checked`.

derivedFrom[].headerType.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example
notes: An `annotates` item must name `FHR`: the schema forces it.

derivedFrom[].relationship.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example
notes: The vocabulary is shared and provisional (FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#54); `annotates` is the relationship that carries the genome link here.

derivedFrom[].checksum.units: standard padded base64 of the parent file's SHA-512/256
derivedFrom[].checksum.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example
notes: This is the checksum of the genome file, not of this GFF3. If it disagrees with the bytes on disk, `verify-links` reports `not matched`.

derivedFrom[].seqcol_id.exampleOmitted: Optional, and no released FHGFF3 example states one for a parent. It is the parent's supplied SeqCol digest, never a substitute for the parent checksum.

derivedFrom[].accessionID.exampleOmitted: Optional, and no released FHGFF3 example states one for a parent. A parent accession alone is not a verified family link.

notes: Non-FAIR-bioHeaders origins of the annotation — an annotation release, evidence set or manual contribution — as asserted by the producer.

source[].name.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example

source[].release.exampleLabel: release naming style from the released family examples

source[].setIdentifier.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example

source[].assemblyAccession.exampleLabel: illustrative value (a real assembly accession shown for its shape)
notes: What the source states for itself; not a link to an FHR file.

source[].sequenceCount.units: sequences or features taken from this source
source[].sequenceCount.exampleLabel: placeholder count from the released family examples

source[].description.example: Short reads used as transcript evidence
source[].description.exampleLabel: value from the released FHGFF3 example

x-<name>.description: Extension field (rule R15): a top-level key the standard does not define, holding any value the producer needs.
notes: Valid from FHGFF3 1.1. Every other unknown key stays invalid, nested objects stay closed, and an `x-` key in a record that states `1.0` is rejected.
Extension fields are covered by the checksum and are omitted from JSON-LD and microdata writers (J9, M5, X9). FHGFF3 has no JSON-LD or microdata form at all today.
The gff3-validator reports header findings and feature findings separately; an extension key is a header finding, never a feature error.

derivedFrom[].accessionID.name.exampleOmitted: Only meaningful inside a `derivedFrom` parent link, which the examples state by checksum. Shape: the parent accession's name, as in `accessionID.name` above.

derivedFrom[].accessionID.url.exampleOmitted: Only meaningful inside a `derivedFrom` parent link, which the examples state by checksum. Shape: a URL resolving to that parent accession.

groups.description: Every field of an FHGFF3 record. The record is a closed object: an unknown top-level key is invalid, with the single exception of the `x-` extension fields listed last.

taxon.title: taxon — the shared core Taxon object
taxon.description: Species name and its identifiers.org taxonomy URI, as in FHR.

metadataAuthor.title: metadataAuthor[] — the shared core Author object
metadataAuthor.description: People or organizations that assert the metadata in this header.

accessionID.title: accessionID — the shared core AccessionID object
accessionID.description: The annotation's own accession, name and URL.

annotationSoftware.title: annotationSoftware[] — the shared Software object
annotationSoftware.description: Software that produced or processed the annotation (schemas/shared.yaml); only `name` is required per entry.

completeness.title: completeness — the shared BUSCO Completeness object
completeness.description: Counts from one BUSCO run against one named lineage dataset (schemas/shared.yaml).
notes: Six members are required whenever the object is present: `lineageDataset`, `completeSingle`, `completeDuplicated`, `fragmented`, `missing` and `total`.

derivedFrom.title: derivedFrom[] — the shared core DerivedFrom object
derivedFrom.description: Parent FAIR-bioHeaders files by checksum. One item, with `headerType: FHR` and `relationship: annotates`, is the annotated genome.
notes: FHGFF3 is the type where the genome link is normative: see the conditional rules below.

featureCounts.title: featureCounts[] — features per type
featureCounts.description: Producer-asserted counts, one entry per feature type.
notes: Only `^\S+$` is checked on `featureType`: the schema does not know the Sequence Ontology, and no count is verified against the file.

genomeReference.title: genomeReference — the declared genome
genomeReference.description: The annotated genome named by assembly accession plus SeqCol digest, when it is not linked by FHR checksum (requirement FR-006).
notes: `accession` and `seqcol_id` are required together whenever the object is present; `assemblyName` is optional.

source.title: source[] — the shared Source object
source.description: Origins of the annotation that are not FAIR-bioHeaders files (schemas/shared.yaml).

at-least-one-genome-link.title: A genome link is required
at-least-one-genome-link.text: At least one genome link is required: a `genomeReference` object, or a `derivedFrom` array holding an item with `headerType: FHR` and `relationship: annotates`. A record with neither is invalid — this is FHGFF3's central conditional rule.

at-most-one-annotates-parent.title: At most one annotated genome
at-most-one-annotates-parent.text: At most one `derivedFrom` item may carry `relationship: annotates`, so a file cannot claim two annotated genomes.

annotates-parent-must-be-FHR.title: `annotates` must name an FHR genome
annotates-parent-must-be-FHR.text: Any `derivedFrom` item with `relationship: annotates` must state `headerType: FHR`: annotation of a transcriptome or protein set is not the genome link this contract requires.

extension-fields-need-the-new-minor.title: Extension fields need the newer minor
extension-fields-need-the-new-minor.text: The schema rejects extension fields in a record that states `schemaVersion: '1.0'`, so a 1.0 record keeps exactly its 1.0 outcome. A record using an extension states `1.1` or a later minor.

extension-fields-allowed.title: Extension fields (rule R15)
extension-fields-allowed.text: Top-level keys matching `^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$` are accepted (rule R15, docs/FORMAT.md) from FHGFF3 1.1, released in shared specification v0.5.0.

closed-top-level.title: The record is a closed object
closed-top-level.text: `additionalProperties: false` — any other unknown top-level key is invalid, and every nested object is closed in the same way.

no-line-feed-in-a-key.title: No key may contain a line feed
no-line-feed-in-a-key.text: `propertyNames` rejects any key containing a line feed, so a YAML continuation artefact cannot pass as part of a field name.

contract.summary: FHGFF3 is the FAIR-bioHeaders header for a GFF3 annotation file. It adds `#~` YAML lines after the `##gff-version 3` line and one SHA-512/256 checksum over the file's exact bytes, and records which genome the coordinates refer to and how the annotation was made. Standalone JSON and YAML carry the same record.
contract.scope: FHGFF3 describes the annotation as a resource. It never makes the features valid: a header says nothing about whether a CDS is in frame or whether the terms are correct, and a GFF3 file without a header is still plain, valid GFF3. Feature and Sequence Ontology validation belongs to the gff3-validator, which reports header findings and feature findings separately.
serializations: GFF3 with a `#~` header block after `##gff-version 3` (optionally `##gff-version 3.x.y`), before the first feature or `##FASTA` line. Native directives such as `##sequence-region` may sit among the header lines.
Standalone JSON and YAML metadata files.
No JSON-LD form and no HTML microdata form exists for FHGFF3 yet: keep the structured record as YAML when exporting a readable HTML table.
tooling: `fair-bioheaders` 0.9.0 (PyPI) bundles the v0.5.0 FHGFF3 schema and reads and writes FHGFF3 1.1, including extension fields, across `combine`, `verify`, `validate`, `convert`, `strip`, `verify-links` and `assess`.

[gff3-validator](https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/gff3-validator) validates GFF3 syntax, Sequence Ontology terms and biology, and reports FHGFF3 header checks (its HDR rules) alongside — never merged with — the feature results. Its header checks run through the toolkit it depends on, and its published 0.1.0 release pins an older `fair-bioheaders`, so a header citing v0.5.0 is reported as an unsupported schema version (HDR-007) rather than checked against FHGFF3 1.1 until that pin is widened. Feature validation does not depend on it.
The browser table builder on this site validates against its documented **v0.4.0** snapshot (`schemaVersion` 1.0), not v0.5.0. Tracked in fair-bioheaders.github.io#15.
caveats: The checksum covers every byte, including native directives, features and any `##FASTA` section, except the root `#~checksum:` line. Sorting or tidying the file (`gt gff3 -sort -tidy`) invalidates a copied header.
`annotation: ""`, `taxon: {}` and `metadataAuthor: []` pass the released schema yet describe nothing; conforming values are non-empty.
`featureCounts`, `soVersion`, `completeness` and `source[]` are producer assertions. The schema checks shapes only: it does not know the Sequence Ontology and does not count features.
A header is not a genome match: `verify-links` compares recorded parent checksums or SeqCol digests against files on disk and reports `matched`, `not matched` or `not checked`.
